subject: Technical deep-dive recap & next steps — StrataIQ deployment scoping
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Mehta <ari@strataiq.com>, Priya Shah <priya@strataiq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: technical deep-dive recap + immediate next steps

Hi Ari / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum. High-level notes:

- Pain / goal: StrataIQ needs sub-200ms p95 inference for single-turn decisioning calls, with peak bursts up to ~1k rps across the fleet. Cost is a secondary constraint but must be predictable for forecasting.
- Model surface: you described a mix of short completions and structured extraction from context windows up to ~8k tokens. You expect ~20% of calls to require longer context pulls (up to ~16k).
- Data / compliance: production traffic will be on a private VPC; SOC2 + audit log retention for 12 months required.

Technical summary / what we discussed:
- Target SLO: 150ms p95 for the 90% of calls that are short; tiered SLO for long-context requests (p95 target 500ms for >8k tokens).
- Topology: Dedicated GPU pool inside a private VPC (Redwood Dedicated) with canary rollout (10% traffic) and automated fallback to a smaller quantized variant if latency spikes or capacity is constrained.
- Batching + caching: continuous request batching with suggested batch cap = 16, and prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes (we estimated 20–30% token savings).
- Model variants: primary: 13B-class chat-optimized model (quantized 4-bit), fallback: 7B quantized; longer-context variant with window up to 16k tokens enabled for a small subset.

Attachments: SLO matrix and draft MAP attached.

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) I’ll share a short SLO matrix and deployment sketch (attached) — action: StrataIQ to confirm whether 16k context is required for 20% of calls or fewer.
2) Security kickoff: Marissa will send the SOC2 questionnaire and onboarding checklist by EOD tomorrow.
3) Pilot: propose a 4-week pilot on Dedicated capacity with a 2-week canary at 10% traffic, then ramp.

Can you confirm the above (especially the long-context percentage) and confirm which email we should use to share the first quote/PO? If you prefer, we can slot a 30-minute follow-up to lock down pilot sizing.

Best,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: technical deep-dive recap + immediate next steps

Connor —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the points below:

- Long-context calls: estimate ~18% of total calls will need >8k tokens (these are enrichment calls where we attach recent user history). We can accept a higher p95 for those longer runs if it’s significantly cheaper.
- SLOs look reasonable; the business wants to be conservative on the short-call p95 (would prefer <=150ms).
- Procurement: please send the pilot quote to procurement@strataiq.com. We will need the SOC2 questionnaire returned before the pilot kicks off.

Quick clarifying Qs from Priya:
1) What does the autoscale profile look like for burst handling? (how fast we can add GPU capacity)
2) If we do the canary, how easy is it to set a rollback threshold by latency vs error rate?

Happy to take a 30-min follow-up on Thursday to finalize sizing.

—Ari
VP Product, StrataIQ
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Mehta <ari@strataiq.com>, Priya Shah <priya@strataiq.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: technical deep-dive recap + immediate next steps

Ari / Priya —

Answers to the two quick questions and a bit more on the deployment plan: 

1) Autoscale for bursts: Dedicated capacity supports policy-driven autoscaling. For your footprint we recommend a baseline pool sized for steady-state QPS and a burst pool that can be spun up within ~90–150 seconds (warmup depends on the chosen model variant and whether warm kernels/weights are resident). We propose pre-warmed standby nodes for critical zones to shorten cold-starts to ~20–30s for the 13B quantized variant.

2) Canary rollback thresholds: you can define multi-metric guardrails — latency (p95) and error rate (5xx). The rollout controller supports automatic rollback when p95 exceeds a configured multiplier of baseline or when error rate crosses an absolute threshold. In a typical canary we use: p95 > 1.25x baseline OR error rate > 0.5% for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows -> auto-rollback.

3) Batching and concurrency: recommended max concurrency per GPU for the 13B quantized variant: 64 concurrent requests with batch cap=16; this gives the best balance for low p95 on short calls and throughput for bursts.

4) KV/prefix cache: we'll enable prefix caching for your enrichment calls; expect ~25% token reduction on repeat patterns.

Next steps from our side: I’ll drop the SOC2 questionnaire and a short pilot runbook (one-pager) to procurement@strataiq.com by EOD. Connor will follow with the pilot quote.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: technical deep-dive recap + immediate next steps

Ari / Priya —

Thanks for the confirmation and the questions. Quick operational commitments and proposed timeline: 

- Quote / PO: Connor will send the pilot quote to procurement@strataiq.com by EOD today. We’ll include line items for Dedicated baseline, pre-warmed standby nodes (optional), and a small pool of long-context variants.
- Security: Marissa will share the SOC2 questionnaire now; once returned we can schedule the security kickoff (we typically slot a 60-minute session to walk the questionnaire).
- Pilot timeline:
  * Week 0: SOC2 questionnaire returned + PO issued -> provisioning starts.
  * Week 1: baseline Dedicated pool provisioned + canary config (10% traffic) in your private VPC.
  * Week 2: canary monitoring window; 2-week pilot begins after go/no-go.
  * Week 4: pilot wrap, capacity/price review, decision point.

Operational notes (short):
- Canary rollback will use the p95 and error-rate thresholds Marissa suggested.
- If the pilot shows latency >150ms p95 on short calls, we will: increase pre-warmed nodes, adjust batching window, or fall back to a slightly smaller model variant and re-run tests.
- We will instrument token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console during the pilot so you can forecast unit economics.

Please confirm that procurement@strataiq.com is the correct PO target and whether you want pre-warmed standby nodes enabled in the pilot (we can mark as optional on the quote). If good, Connor will send the quote and the MAP PDF attached.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
